_comment: Source of truth for pdf_reader_v2. Edit HERE, never in inputs/ or expected/ — those are generated by build_cases.py. Fork of tasks/pdf_reader with two classes of leak removed: (1) answers/computation constants that appeared in the question text, (2) topic hints in the case IDs. `label` is the v1 case id, kept for traceability; it is written only into expected/, which the solution never sees.

cases.label: rent_year2
cases.question: What is the monthly rent in GBP for the second 12 months of the tenancy (months 13-24)?
cases._matcher_fix: v2 originally used leading_numeric here. Every solution that cited its source first — 'Based on clause 1.9b, the rent for 05/09/2023 to 04/09/2024 is GBP 2,100.00' — led with a clause number or a date and was scored wrong while holding the right answer. Measured: 3 of 5 money cases affected across 3 solutions, and mineru beat pdf-inspector by exactly one point purely on word order. currency_amount anchors on the last currency-formatted figure, which is the one being committed to.

cases.label: rent_year3
cases.question: What is the monthly rent in GBP for the third 12 months of the tenancy (months 25-36)? Answer 'N/A' if the fixed term does not extend that far.
cases._deleak: v1 said "Answer 'N/A' if the fixed term is shorter than 36 months", which handed over the term length that case_13 and case_18 both require the model to find for itself.

cases.label: term_start
cases.question: What is the tenancy start date? Format: DD/MM/YYYY.

cases.label: rent_payment_day
cases.question: On what day of the month is the rent payable?
cases.answer: on or prior 5th of the month

cases.label: break_clause
cases.question: Does the tenancy agreement include a contractual break clause allowing the tenant to end the tenancy early without landlord discretion? Answer yes or no.

cases.label: early_surrender
cases.question: Can the tenant request an early surrender of the tenancy subject to landlord approval and associated costs? Answer yes or no.

cases.label: fixed_term_departure_notice
cases.question: If the tenant wants to leave exactly at the end of the fixed term, is notice required? Answer yes or no.

cases.label: post_fixed_term_extension
cases.question: What happens if the tenant remains in the property after the fixed term without signing a new tenancy agreement?
cases.answer: the tenancy automatically extends for six months

cases.label: rent_increase_scope
cases.question: Does the 5% rent increase apply during the original fixed term, the automatic extension period, or both?
cases._deleak: v1 accepted keywords_any ['only','automatic'] — but 'automatic' and 'extension' are both in the question's own list of options, so echoing 'the automatic extension period' scored the case. The discriminating content is the EXCLUSIVITY (extension period but not the fixed term), so the second matcher now requires an exclusivity marker, none of which appear in the question. Gold answer unchanged.
cases._leak_ack: 'extension' must stay in the question — a 3-way multiple choice can't be posed without naming the options. The exclusivity matcher is what makes the case unechoable.

cases.label: deposit_scheme
cases.question: Which tenancy deposit protection scheme is the deposit registered with?

cases.label: pets_allowed
cases.question: Are pets permitted in the property? Answer in one short sentence.
cases._deleak: v1 offered "Answer yes, no, or 'with landlord consent'" — the third option is the answer, and the only non-trivial one on the list.

cases.label: total_rent_fixed_term
cases.question: What is the total rent payable in GBP over the entire fixed term? Show your working and give the final total.
cases._deleak: v1 appended "Compute monthly rent x term length, summing across rent periods if rent changes year-on-year", which told the model that the rent is tiered before it had read the document.

cases.label: late_rent_interest_rate
cases.question: What interest rate applies to late rent payments? Answer exactly as written in the agreement, or 'N/A' if not specified.
cases.answer: 3% per annum above Bank of England base rate
cases._deleak: v1's format example was "(e.g. '3% above Bank of England base rate')" — verbatim the gold answer. The case was passable without opening the PDF. Example dropped entirely; 'exactly as written' carries the format requirement on its own.

cases.label: governing_act
cases.question: Clause 1.13 states which statute this Assured Shorthold Tenancy is created under, and cites a specific section of it. Give the Act name, its year, and that section number, as written (e.g. 'Land Registration Act 2002, Section 27').
cases._deleak: v1's format example was "(e.g. 'Housing Act 1988')" — verbatim the gold answer. Doubly weak: 'Housing Act 1988' is also the textbook answer for any AST, so a model could pass closed-book. Now anchored to clause 1.13's Section 19A, which is document-specific. NOTE: this is the one case whose gold answer changed (added ', Section 19A' + the 19A matcher). Revert both together if you want v1 parity.

cases.label: inventory_referenced
cases.question: Has the tenant been told that an inventory or schedule of condition may be used to assess damage claims at the end of the tenancy? Answer yes or no.

cases.label: deposit_dispute_escalation
cases.question: What happens if the Tenant disputes the proposed deposit deductions and the dispute remains unresolved after reasonable attempts to resolve it?
cases.answer: The dispute may be submitted to the Independent Case Examiner (ICE) for adjudication.

cases.label: scenario_leave_22mo_replacement_1mo_gap
cases.question: The tenant is 22 months into the fixed term and wants to surrender the tenancy immediately. The Landlord agrees, and finds a replacement tenant 1 month later who pays, for each remaining month, the rent this agreement specifies for that month. Using the early-surrender terms in Section 6, calculate the total cost to the surrendering tenant. Include all four of: (a) rent for the 1-month void before the replacement moves in, (b) the Landlord's new letting fee, charged on the replacement tenant's rent for the months the replacement occupies up to the end of the fixed term, (c) the inventory check-in charge, and (d) the Landlord's administration charge. Show your working and give the final GBP total.
cases._deleak: v1 spelled out 'letting fee 13.2%', 'inventory check-in (£144 x months_early / 36)' and 'administration charges (£480 x months_early / 36)' in the question. All four constants (11%+VAT=13.2%, £144, £480) and the 36-month term are stated in Section 6 / clause 1.8 of the PDF — with them in the prompt, the case tested arithmetic only. The four components (a)-(d) are still named so the case stays gradeable against a single total; only the numbers are gone.
cases._ambiguity: The fee BASIS must stay in the question. Section 6 words it as 'of the rent from the date of early surrender until the original end date', which reads as months 23-36 (14 months) and yields 6698.67 — a defensible answer that scores 0. v1 disambiguated with 'on the replacement's rent'; an early v2 draft dropped that qualifier along with the constants and made the case unanswerable-as-graded. The qualifier is a basis, not a constant, so it leaks nothing. Do not remove it again.

cases.label: early_surrender_economic_incentive
cases.question: Per Section 6 of the agreement, if a tenant surrenders early and the Landlord finds a replacement tenant who pays a HIGHER rent than the surrendering tenant's rate, does the surrendering tenant receive any benefit (e.g. a refund or credit) from the increased rent? Answer yes or no and explain briefly.

cases.label: section6_cost_categories
cases.question: Section 6 sets out the categories of cost the Landlord may charge a tenant who surrenders the tenancy early. List every category it specifies. Two of them are scaled rather than charged in full — state what that scaling is based on.
cases.answer: Five categories: rent under the agreement until the new tenancy starts; any shortfall where the replacement tenant pays a lower rent; the Landlord's new letting fee; a share of the inventory clerk's check-in cost; and a share of the Landlord's cost of administering the new tenancy. The last two are scaled by the number of months surrendered early as a percentage of the current fixed term.

values: percentage of the current fixed term

cases._why: case_18 names its four cost components (a)-(d) in the prompt, which buys gradeability against a single number but hands over the 'which charges apply' step. Section 6 actually lists FIVE — case_18 omits the rent-shortfall item, which is £0 in that scenario. This case tests the step case_18 gives away, and a list question grades naturally on keywords where a single-number question cannot.
cases._antishotgun: Listing plausible charges could hit the first five matchers without reading Section 6. The sixth is the guard: the scaling basis ('number of months to be surrendered early as a percentage of the current fixed term') is specific to this document and is not general UK tenancy knowledge. Do not drop that matcher.
